title: Canonical derived direct-image associativity
statement:
Canonical derived direct-image associativity. For every commutative condensed coefficient ring Λ and schemes and maps as in the following Lean statement, {X Y Z T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (h : Z ⟶ T) :
    DirectImageCompositionAssociative Λ f g h. The canonical maps and predicates are those of [def-sfb-derived-direct-image-open-coherence-data].

proof.text: The existing lowerStar_preservesKInjectives instance is supplied by the exact inverse-image/direct-image adjunction. Specialize the proved generic Functor.rightDerivedFunctorCompIso'_assoc in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.FiniteCoefficient.Derived.LowerStarComp to the six module direct-image functors. Use lowerStarComp for the binary comparisons, appending lowerStarCongr (Category.assoc f g h) to the third comparison. The compatibility hypothesis is exactly the componentwise inverse orientation of lowerStarComp_assoc; the functor associator has identity components.

Functoriality of rightDerivedFunctorNatTrans under composition identifies the derived comparison of the appended ordinary compositor with the composite derived comparisons (hpost in the Lean proof). Turn the generic equality of hom transformations into an equality of natural isomorphisms. Take inverse components, cancel the inverse of the derived lowerStarCongr, and unfold directImageComposition. rightDerivedFunctorNatIso of the inverse compositor is the inverse of rightDerivedFunctorNatIso of the compositor by its definition. The derived functor associator has identity components, and lowerStarCongr is precisely eqToIso of congrArg lowerStar along scheme associativity. This gives DirectImageCompositionAssociative with its original signature.

proof_origin.place: Functor.rightDerivedFunctorCompIso'_assoc, specialized directly to the module-object direct images; ordinary coherence is lowerStarComp_assoc. This is the right-adjoint composition argument of the current blueprint sk-thm-sf-comp-composition proof, Canonicity and associativity. No finite-word descent or coefficient admissibility hypothesis is required.
